newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bank task force to be named soon - minister.
newsitem.headline: Canada bank task force to be named soon - minister.

text.p: A government task force to study competition issues in Canada's banking sector will be named within the next few weeks, a senior federal official said on Tuesday.
"I would think in the next couple of weeks. Early November would be the latest," Doug Peters, secretary of state responsible for financial institutions, told reporters.
The so-called Task Force on the Future of the Canadian Financial Services Sector was announced last June when the government released its long-awaited white paper on financial services reforms.
The white paper proposed streamlining regulations in several areas, including allowing some foreign banks to opt out of paying deposit insurance.
But foreign banks are still lobbying for the right to set up branches in Canada with access to their parent firms' capital.
Under current rules, offshore banks must establish a federally regulated subsidiary with its own capital, board of directors and audit system.
The high cost of operating a separately capitalized unit prompted several foreign banks to leave Canada in recent years.

Since June, foreign bankers have lobbied the federal government to include branch banking in the proposed 1997 changes to the Bank Act. Parliament would have to act on the proposals in the white paper by March 31, 1997.
Peters said a decision on the branch issue was not final since any new legislation could be amended.

He said it would take time, however, to draw up new rules to govern foreign bank branches. "I would think you would want the task force to take a look at that issue more so than others," Peters said. The task force will have about 18 months to study these and other competitive issues.
